key_insight: Finite element simulations show how thermally induced bending in NiTi-based bilayer hinges can drive coordinated self-folding of microscale origami for brain implants.
engineering_relevance: Self-folding thin-film structures could support compact delivery and controlled deployment of neurovascular implants in confined vessels.
method: Model thermal-stress-driven bending in NiTi–molybdenum and NiTi–SS316L bilayer hinges.
Optimize hinge length, layer thickness, width, and shape using finite element simulations.
Integrate hinges into a waterbomb origami unit cell to evaluate coordinated folding.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a simulated hinge design enabling approximately 50% smaller unit-cell dimensions than previously reported designs, plus coordinated self-folding in a complete waterbomb unit cell.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation results, not experimental validation of microscale fabrication, deployment, or safe thermal actuation in vivo.
paper_title: Design of Self-Folding Origami Architectures for Biomedical Implants: A Finite Element Simulation Framework
